/**
 * This version is stamped on May 10, 2016
 *
 * Contact:
 *   Louis-Noel Pouchet <pouchet.ohio-state.edu>
 *   Tomofumi Yuki <tomofumi.yuki.fr>
 *
 * Web address: http://polybench.sourceforge.net
 */
/* ludcmp.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "ludcmp.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j;
  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      x[i] = 0;
      y[i] = 0;
      b[i] = (i+1)/fn/2.0 + 4;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_ludcmp[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

  DATA_TYPE w;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] = w / A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
       A[i][j] = w;
    }
  }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     w = b[i];
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * y[j];
     y[i] = w;
  }

   for (i = _PB_N-1; i >=0; i--) {
     w = y[i];
     for (j = i+1; j < _PB_N; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * x[j];
     x[i] = w / A[i][i];
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(b, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_ludcmp (n,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(b);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);

  return 0;
}

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)      # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)      # reduction index over previously computed entries

data:
    # Dense N×N matrix, row-major. After factorization it holds L (strict lower)
    # and U (upper incl. diagonal) in-place.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Right-hand side and solution / temporaries (1D, contiguous).
    b[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    y[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # forward-substitution result
    x[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # backward-substitution result

parameters:
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for blocked LU and trailing updates (chosen per hardware).
    NB_panel:    int  # panel (i) block size for LU factorization
    NB_trail_i:  int  # i tile size for trailing submatrix updates
    NB_trail_j:  int  # j tile size for trailing submatrix updates
    VEC_J:       int  # SIMD width for j-dimension vectorization

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. In-place LU factorization of A (Doolittle, no pivoting).
    #    A initially holds the SPD matrix from init_array.
    #    After this, A holds:
    #      - L in strict lower triangle (implicit unit diagonal),
    #      - U in upper triangle (incl. diagonal).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):          # outer i must be sequential
        # 1.a Compute L(i, j) for j < i  (strict lower triangle)
        #     L(i, j) = (A(i, j) - sum_{k<j} L(i, k) * U(k, j)) / U(j, j)
        for j in [0, i):
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j)) ( A[i, k] * A[k, j] ) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 1.b Compute U(i, j) for j >= i  (upper triangle)
        #     U(i, j) = A(i, j) - sum_{k<i} L(i, k) * U(k, j)
        for j in [i, N):
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j] - sum(k in [0, i)) ( A[i, k] * A[k, j] )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Forward substitution: solve L * y = b
    #    L has unit diagonal stored implicitly.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        y[i] =
            b[i] - sum(j in [0, i)) ( A[i, j] * y[j] )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Backward substitution: solve U * x = y
    #    Executed in decreasing i order: i = N-1, ..., 0.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)) decreasing:   # semantics: process i = N-1 .. 0
        x[i] =
            ( y[i] - sum(j in (i, N)) ( A[i, j] * x[j] ) )
            / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # LU factorization row dependencies:
    #  - Row i depends on all rows < i (both L and U entries).
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 < i2:
        LU_row(i1) -> LU_row(i2)

    # Within the L-part of row i, iteration j depends on all prior j' < j:
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, i), j2 in [0, i), j1 < j2:
        L_update(i, j1) -> L_update(i, j2)

    # Within the U-part of a fixed row i, different j are independent
    # (given all required L(i, k) and previous rows are available).
    # There is no dependency between U_update(i, j1) and U_update(i, j2)
    # for j1 != j2 at fixed i.

    # Forward substitution (L * y = b): y[i] depends on all y[j], j < i.
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 < i2:
        y_update(i1) -> y_update(i2)

    # Backward substitution (U * x = y): x[i] depends on all x[j], j > i.
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 > i2:
        x_update(i1) -> x_update(i2)

optimization:
    # ================================================================
    # High-level algorithmic optimization: blocked right-looking LU
    # ================================================================
    # Replace the purely row-wise LU factorization by an equivalent
    # right-looking *blocked* LU to improve cache reuse and expose
    # coarse-grain parallelism in the trailing submatrix updates.
    #
    # The transformation preserves the algebra:
    #   - Panel factorization within each block uses the same formulas
    #     as in 'computation' and obeys the same dependencies.
    #   - Updates of A[r, c] are merely regrouped (associativity of +, *)
    #     and performed in blocks instead of elementwise.

    # Panel blocking along i (row dimension) for LU factorization.
    block(i, I_panel, NB_panel)
    # For each panel I_panel = [ii, ii+NB_panel):
    #   1. Factor the diagonal block A[ii:ii+NB_panel, ii:ii+NB_panel]
    #      sequentially using the scalar LU loops above (same semantics).
    #   2. Compute block row (U) and block column (L) adjacent to the
    #      diagonal block (Level-2 BLAS-like operations).
    #   3. Update the trailing submatrix A22 = A22 - L21 * U12, which
    #      is GEMM-like and optimized further below.

    # ================================================================
    # Cache/SIMD-friendly blocking for trailing submatrix updates
    # ================================================================
    # The GEMM-like trailing update after each panel has the form:
    #   for i in (panel_end, N):
    #     for j in (panel_end, N):
    #       A[i, j] -= sum(k in panel) A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    #
    # Apply 2D tiling over (i, j) to improve locality and create
    # independent tiles for parallel execution.
    block(i, I_trail, NB_trail_i)   # tile trailing rows
    block(j, J_trail, NB_trail_j)   # tile trailing columns

    # Arrange the innermost loops as:
    #   for I_trail:
    #     for J_trail:
    #       for k in panel:
    #         for j in J_trail (contiguous in memory)
    # to get contiguous access in j and good reuse of A[i, k].
    interchange(J_trail, k)

    # Vectorize and unroll across J_trail in the trailing GEMM-like kernel.
    vectorize(J_trail, VEC_J)
    unroll(J_trail, 4)

    # ================================================================
    # Exploiting parallelism
    # ================================================================
    # LU factorization:
    #   - I_panel (panels) remain sequential due to strong inter-panel
    #     dependencies.
    #   - Within a fixed panel, the U-part loop over j for a given i
    #     has no intra-row dependencies and is amenable to SIMD.
    #
    # Vectorize U-part j-loops (j in [i, N)):
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)    # only for the U update in each row
    unroll(j, 4)

    # Trailing submatrix update tiles (I_trail, J_trail) are independent
    # for a fixed panel. Parallelize over these tiles.
    parallelize(I_trail)
    parallelize(J_trail)

    # Forward and backward substitutions are inherently sequential in i,
    # but their inner j-loops can still be optimized.
    unroll(j, 4)           # for inner j in both solves
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)    # especially for backward solve (j in (i, N))

    # ================================================================
    # Scalar / memory micro-optimizations
    # ================================================================
    # - Hoist row pointers A[i, *] and frequently reused values
    #   (e.g., A[j, j] in L updates) outside inner loops.
    # - Keep accumulator 'w' in registers (already modeled in the code).
    # - Ensure A, b, x, y are aligned to vector width to maximize SIMD efficiency.
    hoist(i)  # hoist i-invariant address arithmetic out of inner loops

--- START OF MODEL: ludcmp-02 ---
domain:
    # Matrix / vector indices
    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)        # reduction index

data:
    # In-place LU factors:
    #   - On and above diagonal (i <= j): U(i,j)
    #   - Below diagonal (i > j):        L(i,j)
    #   with implicit L(i,i) = 1
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

    # Right-hand side b and solution x, intermediate y
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE  = i          # 1D row-major
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # solution of A * x = b
    y[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # temporary for forward substitution

parameters:
    N: int                      # problem size

    # Tuning knobs (no change in mathematical result)
    TJ:   int                   # tile size for j (columns) in LU
    TK:   int                   # tile size for k (inner products) in LU
    TJ_f: int                   # tile size for j in forward substitution
    TJ_b: int                   # tile size for j in backward substitution
    VEC_J: int                  # vector width for j-dimension
    VEC_K: int                  # vector width for k-dimension
    UK:    int                  # unroll factor for k-reductions

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This matches the original nested i–j–k structure exactly:
    #   for i = 0..N-1:
    #     (1) compute L(i,0..i-1)
    #     (2) compute U(i,i..N-1)

    for i in seq([0, N)):
        L_factor:                         # compute strict lower part of row i
            for j in seq([0, i)):         # 0 <= j < i
                # A[i, j] := L(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    / A[j, j]

        U_factor:                         # compute upper part of row i
            for j in seq([i, N)):         # i <= j < N
                # A[i, j] := U(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

    # Forward substitution: solve L * y = b.
    # L has unit diagonal; lower part stored in A(i,j) for j < i.
    Forward:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)), A[i, j] * y[j])

    # Backward substitution: solve U * x = y.
    # U is upper-triangular, stored in A(i,j) for j >= i.
    Backward:
        # descending loop: i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        for i in seq([0, N)) reversed:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)), A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. LU factorization (panel-wise, row i depends on rows 0..i-1)

    # L(i,j) depends on previous entries in the same row (L(i,0..j-1))
    # and on U(k,j) in rows k < j < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):                   # j >= 1
        for k in [0, j):
            L_factor(i, k) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # U(i,j) depends on the entire L(i,0..i-1) and on U(0..i-1, j).
    for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):
        for k in [0, i):
            L_factor(i, k) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # 2. Forward substitution y: y[i] depends on all y[0..i-1]
    #    and on L(i,0..i-1).
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            L_factor(i, j) -> Forward(i)
            Forward(j)     -> Forward(i)

    # 3. Backward substitution x: x[i] depends on x[i+1..N-1]
    #    and on U(i,i..N-1).
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [i+1, N):
            U_factor(i, j) -> Backward(i)
            Backward(j)    -> Backward(i)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level notes:
    #  - Outer loop i must remain sequential for LU and both solves
    #    because each row i depends on all rows < i (and, for x,
    #    on rows > i).
    #  - Inner products (sums over k or j) are true reductions and
    #    are good targets for unrolling, vectorization and partial
    #    blocking.
    #  - For a single right-hand side, parallelism is available
    #    inside the U update (j >= i) but not in the L update (j < i).
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # Keep i as the outermost loop for all phases (LU, forward, backward).
    hoist(i)

    # ---------------- LU factorization ----------------
    # Cache blocking for j and k in both L_factor and U_factor.
    # Tiles are processed in increasing index order to preserve all
    # loop-carried dependencies in the triangular L-part.
    #
    # For each fixed i:
    #   - L_factor: 0 <= j < i, 0 <= k < j
    #   - U_factor: i <= j < N, 0 <= k < i
    #
    # Block j and k to keep active rows and columns of A in L1/L2.
    block(j, J, TJ)     # j = J..min(J+TJ, bound_of_j)
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K..min(K+TK, bound_of_k)

    # Within each j-tile of L_factor, maintain sequential j order.
    # This preserves the dependence of L(i,j) on L(i,0..j-1).

    # Parallelize only the U-part in j (columns) for each fixed i.
    # For U_factor at a given i, updates of U(i,j) for j >= i are
    # independent of each other, so they can be distributed across
    # threads safely.
    #
    #   for fixed i:
    #     for J in tiles of [i, N):
    #       parallel over J:
    #         for j in J:
    #           U(i,j) update ...
    parallelize(J)    # apply only to U_factor j-tiles (j >= i)

    # Vectorize inner products over k and column updates over j
    # where no loop-carried dependencies exist (U_factor and reductions).
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)       # inner reductions in L_factor and U_factor
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)       # U_factor column-wise updates

    # Unroll k to expose more ILP and better use fused-multiply-add (FMA)
    # units in the core.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # ---------------- Forward substitution (Ly = b) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential (triangular dependency on y[0..i-1]).
    # The inner sum over j is a reduction; we can:
    #   - block j for cache,
    #   - vectorize j within each row,
    #   - optionally implement the reduction with a small SIMD micro-kernel.
    block(j, J_f, TJ_f)       # tile j in Forward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Backward substitution (Ux = y) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential in descending order (triangular dependency
    # on x[i+1..N-1]). The inner sum over j is again a reduction.
    block(j, J_b, TJ_b)       # tile j in Backward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Optional extensions (conceptual) --------------
    # - If multiple right-hand sides are available, extend b, x, y to
    #   data structures b[i, r], x[i, r], y[i, r] over an extra
    #   dimension r (RHS index) and:
    #     * parallelize(r)
    #     * vectorize(r, VEC_R)
    #   turning the forward/back substitution into a level-3 BLAS-like
    #   TRSM operation with much higher arithmetic intensity.
    #
    # - On architectures with large caches, TJ and TK can be chosen so
    #   that a panel of several rows of L and a block of columns of U
    #   fit in L2, improving reuse of A[k, j] across different i.
--- END OF MODEL: ludcmp-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: ludcmp-03 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A is stored row-major and overwritten in-place with LU factors:
    #   - L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A
    #   - U is stored in the upper triangle of A (including the diagonal)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Right-hand side and solution vectors
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE    = i -> i
    y[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # forward-substitution result (Ly = b)
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE   = i -> i  # final solution (Ux = y)

    # Optional temporary buffer used only by an optimization that precomputes
    # 1 / A[i, i] to replace divisions by multiplications.
    # Size N << N^2, so extra memory is well below +50% of the original footprint.
    diag_inv[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # holds 1 / A[i, i] when enabled

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix and vector dimension
    TI: int   # tile size for i (row blocking)
    TJ: int   # tile size for j (column blocking)
    TK: int   # tile size for k (reduction blocking)
    VJ: int   # SIMD width for vectorization along j
    UK: int   # unrolling factor for reductions over k

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # On entry:  A contains the original dense matrix.
    # On exit:   A encodes L and U such that A_orig = L * U,
    #            with L unit-diagonal lower-triangular and U upper-triangular.
    LU_factor:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            # Compute strict lower-triangular entries L[i, 0..i-1].
            L_row:
                for j in seq([0, i)):
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j)) A[i, k] * A[k, j] )
                        / A[j, j]

            # Compute upper-triangular entries U[i, i..N-1].
            U_row:
                for j in [i, N):
                    A[i, j] =
                        A[i, j]
                        - sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]

    # Forward substitution: solve L y = b.
    Forward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in [0, i)) A[i, j] * y[j]

    # Backward substitution: solve U x = y.
    # Implemented as a forward sweep in the reversed index r = N-1-i
    # so that the loop variable still increases while respecting dependencies.
    Backward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            x[N - 1 - i] =
                ( y[N - 1 - i]
                  - sum(j in (N - 1 - i + 1, N))
                        A[N - 1 - i, j] * x[j] )
                / A[N - 1 - i, N - 1 - i]

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking / tiling
    # -----------------------------
    # Tile all three logical dimensions involved in the cubic work of LU.
    # The transformation preserves the original lexicographic order of (i, j, k)
    # within each tile, so numerical semantics (up to FP rounding) are unchanged.
    block(i, Ii, TI)   # outer tiles over rows i
    block(j, Jj, TJ)   # outer tiles over columns j
    block(k, Kk, TK)   # outer tiles over reduction dimension k
    hoist(Ii)          # process panels of rows as the outermost loop

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Improve U-row locality via loop interchange
    # -----------------------------
    # For the upper-triangular update (U_row), interchange loops over j and k:
    #
    #   Original (for fixed i):

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. LU factorization without pivoting (in-place in A)
    #    L has unit diagonal; L(i, j) for j < i is stored in A[i, j]
    #    U(i, j) for j >= i is stored in A[i, j]

            U_FACT[i, j]:
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)),
                          A[i, k] * A[k, j])

        # Precompute the reciprocal of the diagonal U(i, i) for later use
        DIAG_INV[i]:
            invD[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

    #    L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------

                - sum(j in seq([0, i)),

    # Factorization is fundamentally sequential in i: row i depends on all rows < i.

    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1+1, N):

    vectorize(j, VK)       # vectorize inner sums in FWD and BWD where legal

        #      Division by U(j,j) replaced by multiplication with D[j].
        #------------------------------------
        FACT_L_ROW[i]:
          for j in seq[0, i):                # j sequential: depends on A[i,0..j-1]

#include <stdio.h>

#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j;
  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      x[i] = 0;
      y[i] = 0;
      b[i] = (i+1)/fn/2.0 + 4;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_ludcmp[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

  DATA_TYPE w;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] = w / A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
       A[i][j] = w;
    }
  }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     w = b[i];
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * y[j];
     y[i] = w;
  }

   for (i = _PB_N-1; i >=0; i--) {
     w = y[i];
     for (j = i+1; j < _PB_N; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * x[j];
     x[i] = w / A[i][i];
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(b, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_ludcmp (n,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(b);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);

  return 0;
}

    # and U (upper incl. diagonal) in-place.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Right-hand side and solution / temporaries (1D, contiguous).
    b[i]: in    DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i
    y[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # forward-substitution result
    x[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i   # backward-substitution result

parameters:
    N: int

    # Tuning parameters for blocked LU and trailing updates (chosen per hardware).
    NB_panel:    int  # panel (i) block size for LU factorization
    NB_trail_i:  int  # i tile size for trailing submatrix updates
    NB_trail_j:  int  # j tile size for trailing submatrix updates
    VEC_J:       int  # SIMD width for j-dimension vectorization

computation:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. In-place LU factorization of A (Doolittle, no pivoting).
    #    A initially holds the SPD matrix from init_array.
    #    After this, A holds:
    #      - L in strict lower triangle (implicit unit diagonal),
    #      - U in upper triangle (incl. diagonal).
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):          # outer i must be sequential
        # 1.a Compute L(i, j) for j < i  (strict lower triangle)
        #     L(i, j) = (A(i, j) - sum_{k<j} L(i, k) * U(k, j)) / U(j, j)
        for j in [0, i):
            A[i, j] =
                ( A[i, j]
                  - sum(k in [0, j)) ( A[i, k] * A[k, j] ) )
                / A[j, j]

        # 1.b Compute U(i, j) for j >= i  (upper triangle)
        #     U(i, j) = A(i, j) - sum_{k<i} L(i, k) * U(k, j)
        for j in [i, N):
            A[i, j] =
                A[i, j] - sum(k in [0, i)) ( A[i, k] * A[k, j] )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Forward substitution: solve L * y = b
    #    L has unit diagonal stored implicitly.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        y[i] =
            b[i] - sum(j in [0, i)) ( A[i, j] * y[j] )

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Backward substitution: solve U * x = y
    #    Executed in decreasing i order: i = N-1, ..., 0.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)) decreasing:   # semantics: process i = N-1 .. 0
        x[i] =
            ( y[i] - sum(j in (i, N)) ( A[i, j] * x[j] ) )
            / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # LU factorization row dependencies:
    #  - Row i depends on all rows < i (both L and U entries).
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 < i2:
        LU_row(i1) -> LU_row(i2)

    # Within the L-part of row i, iteration j depends on all prior j' < j:
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, i), j2 in [0, i), j1 < j2:
        L_update(i, j1) -> L_update(i, j2)

    # Within the U-part of a fixed row i, different j are independent
    # (given all required L(i, k) and previous rows are available).
    # There is no dependency between U_update(i, j1) and U_update(i, j2)
    # for j1 != j2 at fixed i.

    # Forward substitution (L * y = b): y[i] depends on all y[j], j < i.
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 < i2:
        y_update(i1) -> y_update(i2)

    # Backward substitution (U * x = y): x[i] depends on all x[j], j > i.
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [0, N), i1 > i2:
        x_update(i1) -> x_update(i2)

optimization:
    # ================================================================
    # High-level algorithmic optimization: blocked right-looking LU
    # ================================================================
    # Replace the purely row-wise LU factorization by an equivalent
    # right-looking *blocked* LU to improve cache reuse and expose
    # coarse-grain parallelism in the trailing submatrix updates.
    #
    # The transformation preserves the algebra:
    #   - Panel factorization within each block uses the same formulas
    #     as in 'computation' and obeys the same dependencies.
    #   - Updates of A[r, c] are merely regrouped (associativity of +, *)
    #     and performed in blocks instead of elementwise.

    # Panel blocking along i (row dimension) for LU factorization.
    block(i, I_panel, NB_panel)
    # For each panel I_panel = [ii, ii+NB_panel):
    #   1. Factor the diagonal block A[ii:ii+NB_panel, ii:ii+NB_panel]
    #      sequentially using the scalar LU loops above (same semantics).
    #   2. Compute block row (U) and block column (L) adjacent to the
    #      diagonal block (Level-2 BLAS-like operations).
    #   3. Update the trailing submatrix A22 = A22 - L21 * U12, which
    #      is GEMM-like and optimized further below.

    # ================================================================
    # Cache/SIMD-friendly blocking for trailing submatrix updates
    # ================================================================
    # The GEMM-like trailing update after each panel has the form:
    #   for i in (panel_end, N):
    #     for j in (panel_end, N):
    #       A[i, j] -= sum(k in panel) A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    #
    # Apply 2D tiling over (i, j) to improve locality and create
    # independent tiles for parallel execution.
    block(i, I_trail, NB_trail_i)   # tile trailing rows
    block(j, J_trail, NB_trail_j)   # tile trailing columns

    # Arrange the innermost loops as:
    #   for I_trail:
    #     for J_trail:
    #       for k in panel:
    #         for j in J_trail (contiguous in memory)
    # to get contiguous access in j and good reuse of A[i, k].
    interchange(J_trail, k)

    # Vectorize and unroll across J_trail in the trailing GEMM-like kernel.
    vectorize(J_trail, VEC_J)
    unroll(J_trail, 4)

    # ================================================================
    # Exploiting parallelism
    # ================================================================
    # LU factorization:
    #   - I_panel (panels) remain sequential due to strong inter-panel
    #     dependencies.
    #   - Within a fixed panel, the U-part loop over j for a given i
    #     has no intra-row dependencies and is amenable to SIMD.
    #
    # Vectorize U-part j-loops (j in [i, N)):
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)    # only for the U update in each row
    unroll(j, 4)

    # Trailing submatrix update tiles (I_trail, J_trail) are independent
    # for a fixed panel. Parallelize over these tiles.
    parallelize(I_trail)
    parallelize(J_trail)

    # Forward and backward substitutions are inherently sequential in i,
    # but their inner j-loops can still be optimized.
    unroll(j, 4)           # for inner j in both solves
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)    # especially for backward solve (j in (i, N))

    # ================================================================
    # Scalar / memory micro-optimizations
    # ================================================================
    # - Hoist row pointers A[i, *] and frequently reused values
    #   (e.g., A[j, j] in L updates) outside inner loops.
    # - Keep accumulator 'w' in registers (already modeled in the code).
    # - Ensure A, b, x, y are aligned to vector width to maximize SIMD efficiency.
    hoist(i)  # hoist i-invariant address arithmetic out of inner loops

parameters:

    TJ:   int                   # tile size for j (columns) in LU
    TK:   int                   # tile size for k (inner products) in LU
    TJ_f: int                   # tile size for j in forward substitution
    TJ_b: int                   # tile size for j in backward substitution
    VEC_J: int                  # vector width for j-dimension
    VEC_K: int                  # vector width for k-dimension
    UK:    int                  # unroll factor for k-reductions

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This matches the original nested i–j–k structure exactly:
    #   for i = 0..N-1:
    #     (1) compute L(i,0..i-1)
    #     (2) compute U(i,i..N-1)

    for i in seq([0, N)):
        L_factor:                         # compute strict lower part of row i
            for j in seq([0, i)):         # 0 <= j < i
                # A[i, j] := L(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    / A[j, j]

        U_factor:                         # compute upper part of row i
            for j in seq([i, N)):         # i <= j < N
                # A[i, j] := U(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

    # Forward substitution: solve L * y = b.
    # L has unit diagonal; lower part stored in A(i,j) for j < i.
    Forward:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)), A[i, j] * y[j])

    # Backward substitution: solve U * x = y.
    # U is upper-triangular, stored in A(i,j) for j >= i.
    Backward:
        # descending loop: i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        for i in seq([0, N)) reversed:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)), A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. LU factorization (panel-wise, row i depends on rows 0..i-1)

    # L(i,j) depends on previous entries in the same row (L(i,0..j-1))
    # and on U(k,j) in rows k < j < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):                   # j >= 1
        for k in [0, j):
            L_factor(i, k) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # U(i,j) depends on the entire L(i,0..i-1) and on U(0..i-1, j).
    for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):
        for k in [0, i):

            U_factor(k, j) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            L_factor(i, j) -> Forward(i)

    for i in [0, N):

            Backward(j)    -> Backward(i)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level notes:
    #  - Outer loop i must remain sequential for LU and both solves
    #    because each row i depends on all rows < i (and, for x,
    #    on rows > i).
    #  - Inner products (sums over k or j) are true reductions and
    #    are good targets for unrolling, vectorization and partial
    #    blocking.
    #  - For a single right-hand side, parallelism is available
    #    inside the U update (j >= i) but not in the L update (j < i).
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # Keep i as the outermost loop for all phases (LU, forward, backward).
    hoist(i)

    # ---------------- LU factorization ----------------
    # Cache blocking for j and k in both L_factor and U_factor.
    # Tiles are processed in increasing index order to preserve all
    # loop-carried dependencies in the triangular L-part.
    #
    # For each fixed i:
    #   - L_factor: 0 <= j < i, 0 <= k < j
    #   - U_factor: i <= j < N, 0 <= k < i
    #
    # Block j and k to keep active rows and columns of A in L1/L2.
    block(j, J, TJ)     # j = J..min(J+TJ, bound_of_j)
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K..min(K+TK, bound_of_k)

    # This preserves the dependence of L(i,j) on L(i,0..j-1).

    # For U_factor at a given i, updates of U(i,j) for j >= i are

    #     for J in tiles of [i, N):

    vectorize(k, VEC_K)       # inner reductions in L_factor and U_factor
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)       # U_factor column-wise updates

    unroll(k, UK)

    # i must remain sequential (triangular dependency on y[0..i-1]).

    #   - vectorize j within each row,

    block(j, J_f, TJ_f)       # tile j in Forward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    block(j, J_b, TJ_b)       # tile j in Backward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    #   - L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A
    #   - U is stored in the upper triangle of A (including the diagonal)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Right-hand side and solution vectors
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE    = i -> i
    y[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # forward-substitution result (Ly = b)
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE   = i -> i  # final solution (Ux = y)

    # Optional temporary buffer used only by an optimization that precomputes
    # 1 / A[i, i] to replace divisions by multiplications.
    # Size N << N^2, so extra memory is well below +50% of the original footprint.
    diag_inv[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # holds 1 / A[i, i] when enabled

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix and vector dimension
    TI: int   # tile size for i (row blocking)
    TJ: int   # tile size for j (column blocking)
    TK: int   # tile size for k (reduction blocking)
    VJ: int   # SIMD width for vectorization along j
    UK: int   # unrolling factor for reductions over k

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # On entry:  A contains the original dense matrix.
    # On exit:   A encodes L and U such that A_orig = L * U,
    #            with L unit-diagonal lower-triangular and U upper-triangular.
    LU_factor:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            # Compute strict lower-triangular entries L[i, 0..i-1].
            L_row:
                for j in seq([0, i)):
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j)) A[i, k] * A[k, j] )
                        / A[j, j]

            # Compute upper-triangular entries U[i, i..N-1].
            U_row:
                for j in [i, N):
                    A[i, j] =
                        A[i, j]
                        - sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]

    # Forward substitution: solve L y = b.
    Forward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in [0, i)) A[i, j] * y[j]

    # Backward substitution: solve U x = y.
    # Implemented as a forward sweep in the reversed index r = N-1-i
    # so that the loop variable still increases while respecting dependencies.
    Backward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            x[N - 1 - i] =
                ( y[N - 1 - i]
                  - sum(j in (N - 1 - i + 1, N))
                        A[N - 1 - i, j] * x[j] )
                / A[N - 1 - i, N - 1 - i]

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking / tiling
    # -----------------------------
    # Tile all three logical dimensions involved in the cubic work of LU.
    # The transformation preserves the original lexicographic order of (i, j, k)
    # within each tile, so numerical semantics (up to FP rounding) are unchanged.
    block(i, Ii, TI)   # outer tiles over rows i
    block(j, Jj, TJ)   # outer tiles over columns j
    block(k, Kk, TK)   # outer tiles over reduction dimension k
    hoist(Ii)          # process panels of rows as the outermost loop

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Improve U-row locality via loop interchange
    # -----------------------------
    # For the upper-triangular update (U_row), interchange loops over j and k:
    #
    #   Original (for fixed i):
    #       for j in [i, N):
    #           A[i, j] -= sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    #
    #   After interchange:
    #       for k in [0, i):
    #           L_ik = A[i, k]
    #           for j in [i, N):
    #               A[i, j] -= L_ik * A[k, j]
    #
    # This turns U_row into a sequence of rank-1 updates
    #   A[i, i:N) -= L[i, k] * U[k, i:N)
    # over contiguous memory in j (row-major layout), greatly improving
    # cache locality and allowing efficient SIMD across j.
    interchange(U_row.k, U_row.j)

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # -----------------------------
    # Vectorize along the contiguous j-dimension wherever possible:
    #  - inner j-loops of U_row after the interchange
    #  - j-dimension in the sums of the triangular solves (where legal)
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    # Unroll inner reductions over k to increase instruction-level parallelism
    # in both LU_factor and the triangular solves.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Parallelization
    # -----------------------------
    # The outer i-loops in LU_factor and the triangular solves are inherently
    # sequential (each row depends on all previous ones), so we keep i
    # sequential and only parallelize where there is no loop-carried dependence.
    #
    # In U_row, for fixed (i, k) after the interchange, each j-iteration:
    #     A[i, j] -= A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    # is independent of other j-iterations, so j (or its tiled version Jj)
    # can be safely parallelized.
    parallelize(U_row.j)

    # -----------------------------
    # 5. Division elimination via diagonal reciprocals (optional)
    # -----------------------------
    # Custom optimization: precompute reciprocals of the diagonal entries
    # to replace expensive divisions with multiplications.
    #
    #   for i in seq([0, N)):
    #       # After U_row has finalized A[i, i], cache its reciprocal:
    #       diag_inv[i] = 1 / A[i, i]
    #
    # Then rewrite:
    #   - In L_row:
    #       A[i, j] = ( ... ) / A[j, j]
    #     as:
    #       A[i, j] = ( ... ) * diag_inv[j]
    #
    #   - In Backward_substitution:
    #       x[N-1-i] = w / A[N-1-i, N-1-i]
    #     as:
    #       x[N-1-i] = w * diag_inv[N-1-i]
    #
    # This introduces one extra DATA_TYPE[N] buffer (diag_inv), which is
    # negligible compared to the N^2 matrix (well under +50% memory),
    # and removes O(N^3) scalar divisions, replacing them with multiplications.
    # In real arithmetic the result is identical; in floating point only the
    # rounding order changes slightly.
    precompute_diagonal_inverses(A, diag_inv)

domain:

    j:  dim in [0, N)
    k:  dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A initially holds the symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
    # After kernel_ludcmp, A stores L (strict lower triangle, unit diagonal)
    # and U (upper triangle including diagonal) in-place.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # Row-major

    # Right-hand side and solution vectors
    b[i]:    in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i                   # Row-major 1D
    x[i]:    out   DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    y[i]:    inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i

    # Extra temporary: reciprocal of the diagonal of U.
    # Used to replace O(N^2) divisions by O(N) divisions + O(N^2) multiplies.
    invD[i]: temp  DATA_TYPE = i -> i

parameters:
    N:  int      # Problem size, matches runtime n and _PB_N
    TI: int      # Tile size for i (rows) in factorization
    TJ: int      # Tile size for j (columns) in factorization
    TK: int      # Tile size for k (reduction dimension)
    UK: int      # Unroll factor for k
    VK: int      # Vector width (SIMD) for k / j reductions

computation:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. LU factorization without pivoting (in-place in A)
    #    L has unit diagonal; L(i, j) for j < i is stored in A[i, j]
    #    U(i, j) for j >= i is stored in A[i, j]
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        # Compute row i of L in the strict lower triangle: j < i
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            L_FACT[i, j]:
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)),
                            A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    * invD[j]     # invD[j] = 1 / A[j, j]

        # Compute row i of U in the upper triangle including the diagonal: j >= i
        for j in [i, N):
            U_FACT[i, j]:
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)),
                          A[i, k] * A[k, j])

        # Precompute the reciprocal of the diagonal U(i, i) for later use
        DIAG_INV[i]:
            invD[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Forward substitution: solve L * y = b
    #    L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        FWD[i]:
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)),
                      A[i, j] * y[j])

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Backward substitution: solve U * x = y
    #    U is stored in the upper triangle of A including the diagonal.
    #    We use invD[i] instead of dividing by A[i, i].
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([N-1, -1]):   # i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        BWD[i]:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)),
                        A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                * invD[i]      # multiply by 1 / A[i, i] instead of divide

dependencies:
    # Factorization is fundamentally sequential in i: row i depends on all rows < i.

    # Each L_FACT(i2, j) and U_FACT(i2, j) for i2 > i1 need completed row i1

#include <polybench.h>

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j;
  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      x[i] = 0;
      y[i] = 0;
      b[i] = (i+1)/fn/2.0 + 4;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_ludcmp[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

  DATA_TYPE w;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] = w / A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
       A[i][j] = w;
    }
  }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     w = b[i];
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * y[j];
     y[i] = w;
  }

   for (i = _PB_N-1; i >=0; i--) {
     w = y[i];
     for (j = i+1; j < _PB_N; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * x[j];
     x[i] = w / A[i][i];
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(b, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_ludcmp (n,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(b);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);

  return 0;
}

    parallelize(I_trail)
    parallelize(J_trail)

    # but their inner j-loops can still be optimized.
    unroll(j, 4)           # for inner j in both solves
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)    # especially for backward solve (j in (i, N))

domain:

    i: dim in [0, N)        # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)        # column index
    k: dim in [0, N)        # reduction index

data:
    # In-place LU factors:
    #   - On and above diagonal (i <= j): U(i,j)
    #   - Below diagonal (i > j):        L(i,j)
    #   with implicit L(i,i) = 1
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

    # Right-hand side b and solution x, intermediate y
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE  = i          # 1D row-major
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # solution of A * x = b
    y[i]: out DATA_TYPE = i          # temporary for forward substitution

parameters:
    N: int                      # problem size

    # Tuning knobs (no change in mathematical result)
    TJ:   int                   # tile size for j (columns) in LU
    TK:   int                   # tile size for k (inner products) in LU
    TJ_f: int                   # tile size for j in forward substitution
    TJ_b: int                   # tile size for j in backward substitution
    VEC_J: int                  # vector width for j-dimension
    VEC_K: int                  # vector width for k-dimension
    UK:    int                  # unroll factor for k-reductions

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # This matches the original nested i–j–k structure exactly:
    #   for i = 0..N-1:
    #     (1) compute L(i,0..i-1)
    #     (2) compute U(i,i..N-1)

    for i in seq([0, N)):
        L_factor:                         # compute strict lower part of row i
            for j in seq([0, i)):         # 0 <= j < i
                # A[i, j] := L(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)), A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    / A[j, j]

        U_factor:                         # compute upper part of row i
            for j in seq([i, N)):         # i <= j < N
                # A[i, j] := U(i,j)
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)), A[i, k] * A[k, j])

    # Forward substitution: solve L * y = b.
    # L has unit diagonal; lower part stored in A(i,j) for j < i.
    Forward:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)), A[i, j] * y[j])

    # Backward substitution: solve U * x = y.
    # U is upper-triangular, stored in A(i,j) for j >= i.
    Backward:
        # descending loop: i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        for i in seq([0, N)) reversed:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)), A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. LU factorization (panel-wise, row i depends on rows 0..i-1)

    # L(i,j) depends on previous entries in the same row (L(i,0..j-1))
    # and on U(k,j) in rows k < j < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):                   # j >= 1
        for k in [0, j):
            L_factor(i, k) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> L_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # U(i,j) depends on the entire L(i,0..i-1) and on U(0..i-1, j).
    for i in [0, N), j in [i, N):
        for k in [0, i):
            L_factor(i, k) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[i,k] used in sum
            U_factor(k, j) -> U_factor(i, j)        # A[k,j] used in sum

    # 2. Forward substitution y: y[i] depends on all y[0..i-1]
    #    and on L(i,0..i-1).
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            L_factor(i, j) -> Forward(i)
            Forward(j)     -> Forward(i)

    # 3. Backward substitution x: x[i] depends on x[i+1..N-1]
    #    and on U(i,i..N-1).
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [i+1, N):
            U_factor(i, j) -> Backward(i)
            Backward(j)    -> Backward(i)

optimization:
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------
    # High-level notes:
    #  - Outer loop i must remain sequential for LU and both solves
    #    because each row i depends on all rows < i (and, for x,
    #    on rows > i).
    #  - Inner products (sums over k or j) are true reductions and
    #    are good targets for unrolling, vectorization and partial
    #    blocking.
    #  - For a single right-hand side, parallelism is available
    #    inside the U update (j >= i) but not in the L update (j < i).
    # -----------------------------------------------------------------

    # Keep i as the outermost loop for all phases (LU, forward, backward).
    hoist(i)

    # ---------------- LU factorization ----------------
    # Cache blocking for j and k in both L_factor and U_factor.
    # Tiles are processed in increasing index order to preserve all
    # loop-carried dependencies in the triangular L-part.
    #
    # For each fixed i:
    #   - L_factor: 0 <= j < i, 0 <= k < j
    #   - U_factor: i <= j < N, 0 <= k < i
    #
    # Block j and k to keep active rows and columns of A in L1/L2.
    block(j, J, TJ)     # j = J..min(J+TJ, bound_of_j)
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K..min(K+TK, bound_of_k)

    # Within each j-tile of L_factor, maintain sequential j order.
    # This preserves the dependence of L(i,j) on L(i,0..j-1).

    # Parallelize only the U-part in j (columns) for each fixed i.
    # For U_factor at a given i, updates of U(i,j) for j >= i are
    # independent of each other, so they can be distributed across
    # threads safely.
    #
    #   for fixed i:
    #     for J in tiles of [i, N):
    #       parallel over J:
    #         for j in J:
    #           U(i,j) update ...
    parallelize(J)    # apply only to U_factor j-tiles (j >= i)

    # Vectorize inner products over k and column updates over j
    # where no loop-carried dependencies exist (U_factor and reductions).
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)       # inner reductions in L_factor and U_factor
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)       # U_factor column-wise updates

    # Unroll k to expose more ILP and better use fused-multiply-add (FMA)
    # units in the core.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # ---------------- Forward substitution (Ly = b) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential (triangular dependency on y[0..i-1]).
    # The inner sum over j is a reduction; we can:
    #   - block j for cache,
    #   - vectorize j within each row,
    #   - optionally implement the reduction with a small SIMD micro-kernel.
    block(j, J_f, TJ_f)       # tile j in Forward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Backward substitution (Ux = y) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential in descending order (triangular dependency
    # on x[i+1..N-1]). The inner sum over j is again a reduction.
    block(j, J_b, TJ_b)       # tile j in Backward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Optional extensions (conceptual) --------------
    # - If multiple right-hand sides are available, extend b, x, y to
    #   data structures b[i, r], x[i, r], y[i, r] over an extra
    #   dimension r (RHS index) and:
    #     * parallelize(r)
    #     * vectorize(r, VEC_R)
    #   turning the forward/back substitution into a level-3 BLAS-like
    #   TRSM operation with much higher arithmetic intensity.
    #
    # - On architectures with large caches, TJ and TK can be chosen so
    #   that a panel of several rows of L and a block of columns of U
    #   fit in L2, improving reuse of A[k, j] across different i.

    #   - L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A
    #   - U is stored in the upper triangle of A (including the diagonal)
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Right-hand side and solution vectors
    b[i]: in DATA_TYPE    = i -> i
    y[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # forward-substitution result (Ly = b)
    x[i]: out DATA_TYPE   = i -> i  # final solution (Ux = y)

    # Optional temporary buffer used only by an optimization that precomputes
    # 1 / A[i, i] to replace divisions by multiplications.
    # Size N << N^2, so extra memory is well below +50% of the original footprint.
    diag_inv[i]: inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i  # holds 1 / A[i, i] when enabled

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix and vector dimension
    TI: int   # tile size for i (row blocking)
    TJ: int   # tile size for j (column blocking)
    TK: int   # tile size for k (reduction blocking)
    VJ: int   # SIMD width for vectorization along j
    UK: int   # unrolling factor for reductions over k

computation:
    # In-place LU factorization without pivoting.
    # On entry:  A contains the original dense matrix.
    # On exit:   A encodes L and U such that A_orig = L * U,
    #            with L unit-diagonal lower-triangular and U upper-triangular.
    LU_factor:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            # Compute strict lower-triangular entries L[i, 0..i-1].
            L_row:
                for j in seq([0, i)):
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j)) A[i, k] * A[k, j] )
                        / A[j, j]

            # Compute upper-triangular entries U[i, i..N-1].
            U_row:
                for j in [i, N):
                    A[i, j] =
                        A[i, j]
                        - sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]

    # Forward substitution: solve L y = b.
    Forward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in [0, i)) A[i, j] * y[j]

    # Backward substitution: solve U x = y.
    # Implemented as a forward sweep in the reversed index r = N-1-i
    # so that the loop variable still increases while respecting dependencies.
    Backward_substitution:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            x[N - 1 - i] =
                ( y[N - 1 - i]
                  - sum(j in (N - 1 - i + 1, N))
                        A[N - 1 - i, j] * x[j] )
                / A[N - 1 - i, N - 1 - i]

optimization:
    # -----------------------------
    # 1. Cache blocking / tiling
    # -----------------------------
    # Tile all three logical dimensions involved in the cubic work of LU.
    # The transformation preserves the original lexicographic order of (i, j, k)
    # within each tile, so numerical semantics (up to FP rounding) are unchanged.
    block(i, Ii, TI)   # outer tiles over rows i
    block(j, Jj, TJ)   # outer tiles over columns j
    block(k, Kk, TK)   # outer tiles over reduction dimension k
    hoist(Ii)          # process panels of rows as the outermost loop

    # -----------------------------
    # 2. Improve U-row locality via loop interchange
    # -----------------------------
    # For the upper-triangular update (U_row), interchange loops over j and k:
    #
    #   Original (for fixed i):
    #       for j in [i, N):
    #           A[i, j] -= sum(k in [0, i)) A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    #
    #   After interchange:
    #       for k in [0, i):
    #           L_ik = A[i, k]
    #           for j in [i, N):
    #               A[i, j] -= L_ik * A[k, j]
    #
    # This turns U_row into a sequence of rank-1 updates
    #   A[i, i:N) -= L[i, k] * U[k, i:N)
    # over contiguous memory in j (row-major layout), greatly improving
    # cache locality and allowing efficient SIMD across j.
    interchange(U_row.k, U_row.j)

    # -----------------------------
    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling
    # -----------------------------
    # Vectorize along the contiguous j-dimension wherever possible:
    #  - inner j-loops of U_row after the interchange
    #  - j-dimension in the sums of the triangular solves (where legal)
    vectorize(j, VJ)

    # Unroll inner reductions over k to increase instruction-level parallelism
    # in both LU_factor and the triangular solves.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # -----------------------------
    # 4. Parallelization
    # -----------------------------
    # The outer i-loops in LU_factor and the triangular solves are inherently
    # sequential (each row depends on all previous ones), so we keep i
    # sequential and only parallelize where there is no loop-carried dependence.
    #
    # In U_row, for fixed (i, k) after the interchange, each j-iteration:
    #     A[i, j] -= A[i, k] * A[k, j]
    # is independent of other j-iterations, so j (or its tiled version Jj)
    # can be safely parallelized.
    parallelize(U_row.j)

    # -----------------------------
    # 5. Division elimination via diagonal reciprocals (optional)
    # -----------------------------
    # Custom optimization: precompute reciprocals of the diagonal entries
    # to replace expensive divisions with multiplications.
    #
    #   for i in seq([0, N)):
    #       # After U_row has finalized A[i, i], cache its reciprocal:
    #       diag_inv[i] = 1 / A[i, i]
    #
    # Then rewrite:
    #   - In L_row:
    #       A[i, j] = ( ... ) / A[j, j]
    #     as:
    #       A[i, j] = ( ... ) * diag_inv[j]
    #
    #   - In Backward_substitution:
    #       x[N-1-i] = w / A[N-1-i, N-1-i]
    #     as:
    #       x[N-1-i] = w * diag_inv[N-1-i]
    #
    # This introduces one extra DATA_TYPE[N] buffer (diag_inv), which is
    # negligible compared to the N^2 matrix (well under +50% memory),
    # and removes O(N^3) scalar divisions, replacing them with multiplications.
    # In real arithmetic the result is identical; in floating point only the
    # rounding order changes slightly.
    precompute_diagonal_inverses(A, diag_inv)

domain:

    j:  dim in [0, N)
    k:  dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A initially holds the symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
    # After kernel_ludcmp, A stores L (strict lower triangle, unit diagonal)
    # and U (upper triangle including diagonal) in-place.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j      # Row-major

    # Right-hand side and solution vectors
    b[i]:    in    DATA_TYPE = i -> i                   # Row-major 1D
    x[i]:    out   DATA_TYPE = i -> i
    y[i]:    inout DATA_TYPE = i -> i

    # Extra temporary: reciprocal of the diagonal of U.
    # Used to replace O(N^2) divisions by O(N) divisions + O(N^2) multiplies.
    invD[i]: temp  DATA_TYPE = i -> i

parameters:
    N:  int      # Problem size, matches runtime n and _PB_N
    TI: int      # Tile size for i (rows) in factorization
    TJ: int      # Tile size for j (columns) in factorization
    TK: int      # Tile size for k (reduction dimension)
    UK: int      # Unroll factor for k
    VK: int      # Vector width (SIMD) for k / j reductions

computation:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. LU factorization without pivoting (in-place in A)
    #    L has unit diagonal; L(i, j) for j < i is stored in A[i, j]
    #    U(i, j) for j >= i is stored in A[i, j]
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        # Compute row i of L in the strict lower triangle: j < i
        for j in seq([0, i)):
            L_FACT[i, j]:
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in seq([0, j)),
                            A[i, k] * A[k, j]) )
                    * invD[j]     # invD[j] = 1 / A[j, j]

        # Compute row i of U in the upper triangle including the diagonal: j >= i
        for j in [i, N):
            U_FACT[i, j]:
                A[i, j] =
                    A[i, j]
                    - sum(k in seq([0, i)),
                          A[i, k] * A[k, j])

        # Precompute the reciprocal of the diagonal U(i, i) for later use
        DIAG_INV[i]:
            invD[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Forward substitution: solve L * y = b
    #    L has unit diagonal, stored in the strict lower triangle of A.
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([0, N)):
        FWD[i]:
            y[i] =
                b[i]
                - sum(j in seq([0, i)),
                      A[i, j] * y[j])

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Backward substitution: solve U * x = y
    #    U is stored in the upper triangle of A including the diagonal.
    #    We use invD[i] instead of dividing by A[i, i].
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    for i in seq([N-1, -1]):   # i = N-1, N-2, ..., 0
        BWD[i]:
            x[i] =
                ( y[i]
                  - sum(j in seq([i+1, N)),
                        A[i, j] * x[j]) )
                * invD[i]      # multiply by 1 / A[i, i] instead of divide

dependencies:
    # Factorization is fundamentally sequential in i: row i depends on all rows < i.

    # Each L_FACT(i2, j) and U_FACT(i2, j) for i2 > i1 need completed row i1
    # (both U row i1 and its diagonal reciprocal).
    for i1 in [0, N), i2 in [i1+1, N):
        DIAG_INV[i1] -> L_FACT[i2, j]   # access A[*, j] from row i1
        DIAG_INV[i1] -> U_FACT[i2, j]   # access A[*, j] from row i1

    # For a fixed row i, the L update (j < i) must complete before any U update.
    for i in [0, N):
        for jU in [i, N):
            L_FACT[i, jL] -> U_FACT[i, jU]    # jL ranges over [0, i)

    # invD[i] must be ready before any later use of 1 / A[i, i]
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_INV[i] -> L_FACT[i2, j]   where i2 in [i+1, N) and j in [0, i2)
        DIAG_INV[i] -> BWD[i]          # x[i] uses invD[i]

    # Forward substitution Ly = b is strictly sequential in i (y[i] depends on y[0..i-1]).
    for i in [1, N):
        FWD[i-1] -> FWD[i]

    # Forward substitution starts only after LU is available.
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_INV[j] -> FWD[i]  # for all j in [0, i], conservatively

    # Backward substitution Ux = y starts after forward substitution completes.
    for i in [0, N):
        FWD[i] -> BWD[i]

    # Backward substitution is strictly sequential in i in reverse direction:
    # x[i] depends on x[j] for all j > i.
    for i in [0, N-1), j in [i+1, N):
        BWD[j] -> BWD[i]

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Loop tiling for the O(N^3) LU factorization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Tile i, j, k to operate on submatrices that fit better in cache.
    # Tiling preserves the increasing order in i to respect factorization
    # dependencies across rows.
    block(i, Ii, TI)       # i = Ii * TI + ii
    block(j, J, TJ)        # j = J  * TJ + jj
    block(k, K, TK)        # k = K  * TK + kk
    hoist(Ii)              # outermost tile loop over row blocks
    hoist(J)               # next tile loop over column blocks

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Within each fixed row i, the U update loop over j in [i, N) has
    # no loop-carried dependencies (each iteration reads shared A[i, k],
    # A[k, j] and writes a distinct A[i, j]), so it can be parallelized.
    # L update (j < i) is left sequential because it carries dependencies
    # along j through A[i, k].
    parallelize(j)         # applied only to U_FACT[i, j] (j in [i, N))

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # SIMD and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The k-dimension reductions in L_FACT and U_FACT are the innermost
    # arithmetic hot spots. Unroll and vectorize along k to increase ILP
    # and utilize SIMD FMA units.
    unroll(k, UK)          # unroll k in both L_FACT and U_FACT sums
    vectorize(k, VK)       # vector reduction over k (A[i, k] contiguous)

    # The inner sums in forward/backward substitution can likewise be
    # vectorized; they are short but still benefit from SIMD.
    vectorize(j, VK)       # vectorize inner sums in FWD and BWD where legal

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Arithmetic optimization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Using invD[i] replaces O(N^2) scalar divisions (in both L_FACT and BWD)
    # with O(N^2) multiplications and only O(N) divisions to form invD[i],
    # which is significantly cheaper on modern CPUs.

computation:

        #      Division by U(j,j) replaced by multiplication with D[j].

          for j in seq[0, i):                # j sequential: depends on A[i,0..j-1]

        #

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array (int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j;
  DATA_TYPE fn = (DATA_TYPE)n;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      x[i] = 0;
      y[i] = 0;
      b[i] = (i+1)/fn/2.0 + 4;
    }

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  /* not necessary for LU, but using same code as cholesky */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n))

{
  int i;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("x");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    if (i % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, x[i]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("x");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_ludcmp[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(b,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(x,N,n),
		   DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(y,N,n))
{
  int i, j, k;

  DATA_TYPE w;

#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
    for (j = 0; j <i; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
        A[i][j] = w / A[j][j];
    }
   for (j = i; j < _PB_N; j++) {
       w = A[i][j];
       for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
          w -= A[i][k] * A[k][j];
       }
       A[i][j] = w;
    }
  }

  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     w = b[i];
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * y[j];
     y[i] = w;
  }

   for (i = _PB_N-1; i >=0; i--) {
     w = y[i];
     for (j = i+1; j < _PB_N; j++)
        w -= A[i][j] * x[j];
     x[i] = w / A[i][i];
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(b, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(x, DATA_TYPE, N, n);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(y, DATA_TYPE, N, n);


  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_ludcmp (n,
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(b),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x),
		 POLYBENCH_ARRAY(y));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(x)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(b);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(x);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(y);

  return 0;
}

    # loop-carried dependencies in the triangular L-part.
    #
    # For each fixed i:
    #   - L_factor: 0 <= j < i, 0 <= k < j
    #   - U_factor: i <= j < N, 0 <= k < i
    #
    # Block j and k to keep active rows and columns of A in L1/L2.
    block(j, J, TJ)     # j = J..min(J+TJ, bound_of_j)
    block(k, K, TK)     # k = K..min(K+TK, bound_of_k)

    # Within each j-tile of L_factor, maintain sequential j order.
    # This preserves the dependence of L(i,j) on L(i,0..j-1).

    # Parallelize only the U-part in j (columns) for each fixed i.
    # For U_factor at a given i, updates of U(i,j) for j >= i are
    # independent of each other, so they can be distributed across
    # threads safely.
    #
    #   for fixed i:
    #     for J in tiles of [i, N):
    #       parallel over J:
    #         for j in J:
    #           U(i,j) update ...
    parallelize(J)    # apply only to U_factor j-tiles (j >= i)

    # Vectorize inner products over k and column updates over j
    # where no loop-carried dependencies exist (U_factor and reductions).
    vectorize(k, VEC_K)       # inner reductions in L_factor and U_factor
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)       # U_factor column-wise updates

    # Unroll k to expose more ILP and better use fused-multiply-add (FMA)
    # units in the core.
    unroll(k, UK)

    # ---------------- Forward substitution (Ly = b) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential (triangular dependency on y[0..i-1]).
    # The inner sum over j is a reduction; we can:
    #   - block j for cache,
    #   - vectorize j within each row,
    #   - optionally implement the reduction with a small SIMD micro-kernel.
    block(j, J_f, TJ_f)       # tile j in Forward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Backward substitution (Ux = y) ----------------
    # i must remain sequential in descending order (triangular dependency
    # on x[i+1..N-1]). The inner sum over j is again a reduction.
    block(j, J_b, TJ_b)       # tile j in Backward
    vectorize(j, VEC_J)

    # ---------------- Optional extensions (conceptual) --------------
    # - If multiple right-hand sides are available, extend b, x, y to
    #   data structures b[i, r], x[i, r], y[i, r] over an extra
    #   dimension r (RHS index) and:
    #     * parallelize(r)
    #     * vectorize(r, VEC_R)
    #   turning the forward/back substitution into a level-3 BLAS-like
    #   TRSM operation with much higher arithmetic intensity.
    #
    # - On architectures with large caches, TJ and TK can be chosen so
    #   that a panel of several rows of L and a block of columns of U
    #   fit in L2, improving reuse of A[k, j] across different i.
--- END OF MODEL: ludcmp-02 ---
